note: Robotics routes at each of the 13 schools: a dedicated BS in robotics where one exists, the ECE route, and the CS route, with the recommended route for a Fall 2027 entrant. Researched 13 October 2026 from each university's own catalog, department and admissions pages; every route carries its source links. Where a fact could not be confirmed it is null or flagged in the notes.

carnegie-mellon.name: Carnegie Mellon University
carnegie-mellon.recommended_summary: Apply to the School of Computer Science, say in the essay that the B.S. in Robotics is the goal, and declare it at the end of first year.

bs_robotics.home_unit: Robotics Institute, School of Computer Science
bs_robotics.entry: High-school applicants must first be admitted to the School of Computer Science and should mention robotics in the essay. SCS first-years declare the BSR at the end of first year, after the spring mini-course 16-180 Concepts in Robotics.
bs_robotics.notes: Launched Fall 2023 as a primary major. CMU's launch announcement expected about 25 students a year; no cap or GPA rule is published for SCS first-years. Students in other CMU colleges can transfer in only in limited numbers, after sophomore year and six core robotics courses. Not ABET-accredited (CMU's ABET list covers its engineering degrees, not SCS).

ece.home_unit: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, College of Engineering
ece.entry: Applicants to the College of Engineering are admitted directly to a department such as ECE, or as undecided.
ece.notes: ECE has five areas of concentration (Device Science and Nanofabrication, Signals and Systems, Circuits, Hardware Systems, Software Systems); none is named robotics. Controls sits in Signals and Systems and embedded systems in Software Systems. Robotics depth comes from adding the Additional Major in Robotics.

cs.entry: Direct admission to the School of Computer Science at application; SCS students can move between SCS majors from spring of sophomore year.
cs.notes: The same SCS admission also opens the BS in Robotics, so CS is the fallback inside the same door rather than a separate application.

robotics_minor.name: Additional Major in Robotics (also a Minor in Robotics; Concentration in Robotics for SCS)
robotics_minor.open_to: Any CMU undergraduate in any college; application needs a 3.0 GPA, windows open each fall and spring.

carnegie-mellon.ecosystem: The Robotics Institute is the largest university robotics research unit in the US; undergrads join through RI labs, the Roboclub, and Mars/lunar rover projects.
carnegie-mellon.tradeoff: SCS is CMU's most selective door, so betting on the BSR means betting on the hardest admission; ECE in Engineering plus the Additional Major in Robotics is the backup inside CMU.
corrections_to_existing: The BSR is not a direct first-year admit: students are admitted to SCS and declare at the end of first year (RI How To Apply page).
ECE's areas of concentration have no robotics area; controls and embedded courses sit in Signals and Systems and Software Systems.

cornell.name: Cornell University
cornell.recommended_summary: Apply to Cornell Engineering with Electrical and Computer Engineering as the intended major and add the Robotics minor; ECE lists robotics as a concentration, cross-lists the core robotics courses, and has a milder affiliation gate than CS.

bs_robotics.notes: Cornell Robotics says plainly that there is no robotics major at present. Students interested in robotics usually major in CS, ECE, Information Science or Mechanical Engineering and take the Robotics minor.

ece.home_unit: Cornell Duffield College of Engineering, School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
ece.robotics_track: Robotics concentration area (one of the ECE concentration areas named in the catalog; power systems and control is another)
ece.entry: Apply to Cornell Engineering (the college, not a major) and list ECE as the intended major. Affiliate with ECE in sophomore year after earning at least C+ in MATH 2930/2940, PHYS 2213 and one ECE gateway course, with a 2.5 GPA across those courses.
ece.notes: The concentration areas appear to be advising areas listed in the catalog, not a transcripted track. ECE 4770 is the same class as CS 4750/MAE 4760; ECE 4160 is the same class as MAE 4190; ECE 4180 is the same class as CS 4758/MAE 4180. ECE 4760 also satisfies the Culminating Design Experience. The ECE major page says the major is chosen in the third semester, while the Engineering admissions FAQ says the second semester of sophomore year; the catalog requires affiliation by the start of the fifth semester.

degree_names: BS Computer Science (Duffield College of Engineering)
BA Computer Science (College of Arts and Sciences)
cs.home_unit: Department of Computer Science, Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science (degree housed in Duffield Engineering or Arts and Sciences)
cs.entry: Apply to Cornell Engineering (for the BS) or Arts and Sciences (for the BA); admission is to the college, not the major. Affiliate in sophomore year with at least C in all CS and critical math courses, a 2.50 average in CS 2110 and CS 2800, and a 2.30 math average.
cs.notes: No formal robotics track or concentration in the CS major; robotics comes through electives and the Robotics minor. The catalog says Engineering students also submit a supplemental application with the affiliation form, but the CS department's own affiliation page does not mention one. Cornell's CS robotics group site now redirects to the university-wide Cornell Robotics site.

robotics_minor.name: Robotics Minor
robotics_minor.open_to: All undergraduates in any college, except students completing the ECE, Mechanical Engineering or CS minors. Six courses: three Fundamentals (Group A) plus three in one specialization (Intelligence; Modeling, Dynamics, and Control; Perception; or Systems and Design), each with C or better. Administered through the Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering.

cornell.ecosystem: Cornell Robotics (robotics.cornell.edu) links robotics faculty across CS, ECE, MAE and Information Science, and robotics-related Engineering project teams include Cornell Mars Rover, Cornell University Autonomous Underwater Vehicle and Combat Robotics @ Cornell.
cornell.tradeoff: ECE spends more required credits on circuits, electromagnetics and microelectronics and has no formal robotics track, so the robotics depth depends on choosing the minor and electives well.
corrections_to_existing: Robotics minor specializations are Intelligence; Modeling, Dynamics, and Control; Perception; and Systems and Design, not 'Foundations / Autonomy / Systems and Design' as stated in robotics_curriculum_detail.

MAE is not direct-admit inside Cornell Engineering: all Engineering students enter without a major and affiliate with any major (MAE, ECE or CS) in sophomore year, so the claim 'MAE is direct-admit within Cornell Engineering' is wrong.
Foundations of Robotics is cross-listed as CS 4750 / ECE 4770 / MAE 4760, so it is available inside both the CS and ECE routes, not only as an MAE course.
The CS 'supplemental application' requirement appears only in the catalog page; the CS department's affiliation page lists only grade thresholds and the affiliation portal. Treat it as unconfirmed.
ECE robotics course list should include ECE 4770 Foundations of Robotics and ECE 4180 Autonomous Mobile Robots (cross-listed ECE numbers) alongside ECE 4160 Fast Robots.

duke.name: Duke University
duke.recommended_summary: Apply to the Pratt School of Engineering and plan to declare the BSE in Electrical and Computer Engineering, adding the Robotics & Automation Undergraduate Certificate, because Duke has no robotics bachelor's and ECE gives the controls, embedded and robotics prerequisites (ECE 280L for ECE 383L) that the certificate builds on.

bs_robotics.notes: Duke has no undergraduate robotics degree. Pratt's majors are Biomedical, Civil, Electrical & Computer, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering, plus the self-designed IDEAS major; robotics appears only as a Mechatronics study area in ME. The only robotics degree is the graduate Robotics & Autonomy Master of Engineering. Undergrads get robotics through the Robotics & Automation Undergraduate Certificate.

degree_names: Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE) in Electrical and Computer Engineering
ece.home_unit: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Pratt School of Engineering
ece.entry: Apply to the Pratt School of Engineering on the Common App (Duke says neither Pratt nor Trinity is easier to get into). Pratt students declare their major in the summer after first year, and no GPA cutoff or cap for ECE is published.
ece.notes: Admission is to Pratt, not to the ECE major; declaration is an open form, not a competitive gate. ECE has no robotics concentration: its two formal concentrations are Machine Learning and Software Engineering, and controls sits inside the 'signal processing, communications, and control systems' elective area. The ML concentration lists ME 555/ECE 590 Robot Learning as an approved free elective. ECE 383L requires ECE 280L or EGR 224L, which ECE majors already take. The BSE needs at least 34 units, with six foundation courses (COMPSCI 201, ECE 110L, 230L, 250D, 270DL, 280L) and at least one design elective. Pratt's Mechanical Engineering major (Mechatronics study area) is a close alternative inside the same school.

degree_names: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
cs.home_unit: Department of Computer Science, Trinity College of Arts & Sciences
cs.entry: Apply to Trinity College of Arts & Sciences; CS is not offered in Pratt. Students declare the major by sophomore spring (the department calls that the ideal time), with no published GPA cutoff or cap.
cs.notes: Admission is to Trinity, not to the CS major; declaring is open. The BS has optional concentrations (AI and Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Systems, Software Engineering and Design) but none in robotics. Fall 2026 matriculants must take an AI core course (e.g., COMPSCI 370 or 371 or 527). COMPSCI 590 Robot Learning is a special topic, not a regular course. Trinity students can earn the robotics certificate, but its required ECE 383L needs ECE 280L or EGR 224L, which are engineering courses outside the CS major.

robotics_minor.name: Robotics & Automation Undergraduate Certificate
robotics_minor.open_to: Duke undergraduates in any school (Pratt or Trinity); 7 courses, coordinated by MEMS

duke.ecosystem: Duke Robotics is a cross-school program (est. 2014) linking robotics labs in MEMS, ECE and CS (e.g., the labs of Boyuan Chen and Leila Bridgeman), and the main undergrad team is the Duke Robotics Club, which builds autonomous underwater vehicles for RoboSub.
duke.tradeoff: Duke has no robotics major or ECE robotics concentration, so the robotics depth comes mostly from the certificate, whose core courses (Robot Studio, robotics ethics, many electives) are ME 555 special topics run by Mechanical Engineering rather than ECE.
corrections_to_existing: Pratt offers six majors, not five: IDEAS (Interdisciplinary Engineering & Applied Science) is also a Pratt major.
The robotics certificate page now lists only Xianyi Cheng as coordinator (Siobhan Rigby Oca no longer listed).
ECE 383's bulletin code is ECE 383L, 'Introduction to Robotics and Automation' (2026-27 bulletin); prerequisite ECE 280L or EGR 224L.

Robotics certificate electives have grown: Controls & Dynamics also includes PHYSICS 361 Intermediate Mechanics and ME 555 Model Predictive Control; Machine Learning also includes ME 555 Data Driven Dynamical Systems and Control and BME 548L Machine Learning and Imaging; Technical electives also include ECE 496/590/ME 555 Rainforest Engineering; there is also a required Humanities & Social Sciences course.
The Duke Robotics course list gives Dynamics as EGR 244L, not EGR 244.
ECE has two undergraduate concentrations (Machine Learning and Software Engineering); neither is robotics. The listed 'ECE 495.08 Introduction to Robotics' could not be found on current Duke pages.
Pratt students declare the major in the summer after first year (bulletin: strongly encouraged before sophomore fall registration, required by junior fall registration).

georgia-tech.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
georgia-tech.recommended_summary: Apply with Computer Engineering (or Electrical Engineering) as the primary major and plan on the Robotics & Autonomous Systems thread, because GT has no robotics BS, the ECE thread gives a formal controls-plus-robotics core, and ECE stays reachable by internal change of major while CS does not.

bs_robotics.notes: Georgia Tech has no bachelor's degree in robotics. IRIM's site lists only a Ph.D. and an M.S. in Robotics. Undergraduates reach robotics through an ECE or CS thread, the ME Automation and Robotic Systems concentration, and the Minor in Robotics.

ece.home_unit: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, College of Engineering
ece.robotics_track: Robotics & Autonomous Systems thread (each student picks two threads; EE pairs it with six other threads, CmpE pairs it with Cybersecurity, Computing Hardware & Emerging Architectures, or Distributed System & Software Design)
ece.entry: First-years do not apply to a college; they list an intended primary major on the Common App, and GT weighs that choice in review. Admitted students confirm their major by May 15, and students can later make one unrestricted major change before 60 credit hours.
ece.notes: The thread requires ECE 3550 and ECE 4550, plus one of ECE 3084, 3251, 4252, 4560, 4580, 4570 or 4575, and one ECE 3000/4000 elective. CmpE students must also add ECE 2026. GT does not publish admit rates by major or college.

cs.robotics_track: Devices + Intelligence threads (no formal robotics track; this is the robotics-leaning thread pairing)
cs.entry: Apply with Computer Science as the primary major on the Common App; the major is weighed in review. First-years admitted Summer 2024 or later cannot change into the BS in CS later, so listing CS at application is the only door.
cs.notes: In the Embedded Devices & AI pairing, CS 3630 satisfies both Devices in the Real World and Embodied Intelligence, and CS 4649 and CS 4476 are Approaches to Intelligence options. CS 4649 is published with the abbreviated title shown. All required CS courses need a C or better.

robotics_minor.name: Minor in Robotics
robotics_minor.open_to: Students in any major; 15 hours: one core course (CS 3630, ECE 4560, ME 4451 or BMED 4739) plus 12 elective hours, at least two courses outside the home school, applied for through ECE.

georgia-tech.ecosystem: The Institute for Robotics and Intelligent Machines (IRIM) is the campus robotics hub, undergraduates can do robotics research for credit through Vertically Integrated Projects (VIP), and RoboJackets fields BattleBots, RoboNav, RoboCup, RoboRacing and RoboWrestling teams.
georgia-tech.tradeoff: Choosing ECE closes the door to the BS in CS, since first-years admitted after Summer 2024 cannot switch into it, so the robotics AI and planning side (CS 3630, CS 4649) has to come through electives or the Robotics minor.
corrections_to_existing: No robotics BS exists, but the existing recommendation (CS with AI + Systems and Architecture threads) is not robotics-oriented; the robotics-relevant CS pairing is Embedded Devices & Artificial Intelligence, which includes CS 3630, CS 4649 and CS 4476.
Calling CS access 'DIRECT, no internal gate' is misleading: first-years admitted Summer 2024 or later cannot change their major to the BS in CS, so CS must be the primary major listed at application.

The claimed first-year admit rates (College of Computing 8.5% vs College of Engineering 13.1%, cited to catalog.gatech.edu) could not be verified. GT's 2025 admitted-student profile gives no admit rates by college; it shows only shares of admits by college (Computing 16%, Engineering 44%).

ME change of major is not a 2.5 GPA threshold. ME requires a 3.0 Georgia Tech GPA plus set courses, but students who started at GT as first-years are exempt if they change within their first two semesters.

Robotics minor elective titles are wrong: AE 4552 is 'Introduction to Humans & Autonomy' (not Autonomous Systems), ECE 4555 is 'Embedded and Hybrid Control Systems', and CS 4476 is 'Introduction to Computer Vision'.

The ECE thread is named 'Robotics & Autonomous Systems' in both the EE and CmpE catalogs, not 'Robotics' for EE. CmpE offers it in three pairings (with Cybersecurity, Computing Hardware & Emerging Architectures, or Distributed System & Software Design).

johns-hopkins.name: Johns Hopkins University
johns-hopkins.recommended_summary: Apply listing Electrical Engineering (or Computer Engineering) as the intended major, then follow the ECE Robotics focus area and add the LCSR Robotics minor, since no robotics BS exists and ECE's catalog focus area already combines controls, embedded systems, perception, and CS/ME robotics courses.

bs_robotics.notes: No undergraduate robotics major exists. JHU admissions lists robotics only as a minor run by LCSR. The LCSR 'BS/MSE' is not a robotics bachelor's. It is a combined five-year program: a current JHU undergrad in any major applies in the fall of junior or senior year, or the summer after, for the MSE in Robotics. Up to two courses count toward both degrees. Whiting's Dean's Master's Fellowship pays 50% of tuition for up to four graduate semesters after the bachelor's. LCSR does not publish a GPA minimum, but ECE says its own combined program expects a 3.5 GPA.

ece.home_unit: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Whiting School of Engineering
ece.robotics_track: Robotics study focus area (optional; one of seven ECE focus areas listed in the 2026-27 catalog for both BS EE and BS CompE)
ece.entry: JHU admits students to the whole university, not to a major. Biomedical Engineering is the only exception. A first-year declares EE or CompE after enrolling. There is no published GPA cap or capacity gate.
ece.notes: Both BS degrees require 126 credits under the 2026-27 catalog for Fall 2026 entrants. The Robotics focus area list also pulls in EN.530.420 Robot Sensors/Actuators, EN.530.421 Mechatronics, EN.601.461 Computer Vision and EN.601.463 Algorithms for Sensor-Based Robotics. Those count as the 'Other Engineering' courses the degree requires (at least 6 credits). They also meet the minor's rule of 6+ credits from outside the home department. Introduction to Mechatronics is listed as 520.240 on the focus-area page but as 520.241 on an instructor page. Its exact code is unverified, so it is left out of key_courses. Admission does not bind you to a major, so 'ECE' here means the intended major listed on the application.

cs.home_unit: Department of Computer Science, Whiting School of Engineering
cs.robotics_track: Robotics focus area (optional; the department also publishes a 'Robotics Path' guide and worksheet)
cs.entry: Students are admitted to the university, then declare CS through an SIS request, a four-year plan on the CS worksheet, and approval from the department and their advisor. No GPA cutoff is published.
cs.notes: The BS requires 120 credits and is accredited by ABET's Computing Accreditation Commission. The BA is open only to students who entered before 2025. The CS robotics courses cover algorithms, vision and AI. Controls and kinematics/dynamics, both required core areas of the minor, have to come from ECE or ME courses.

robotics_minor.name: Robotics Minor (Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics)
robotics_minor.open_to: Any JHU undergraduate in any department. It requires 18 credits at the 300 level or above, covering kinematics/dynamics, systems/control, and computation/sensing, with 3+ lab credits and 6+ credits outside the home department.

johns-hopkins.ecosystem: The Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics (LCSR) anchors robotics at JHU, with medical robotics as a major strength. Undergrad teams include the Johns Hopkins Robotics Club, whose members can get access to the LCSR Robotorium, and the Hopkinauts Mars Rover Team, which competes in the University Rover Challenge.
johns-hopkins.tradeoff: There is no robotics degree on the diploma, and ECE puts little weight on mechanical kinematics/dynamics. He would need ME courses such as EN.530.420/421 to fill that part of the minor, inside a fairly full 126-credit plan.
corrections_to_existing: Existing ECE field says 'No formal ECE robotics track'. Wrong: the 2026-27 catalog lists an optional 'Robotics' study focus area for both BS Electrical Engineering and BS Computer Engineering.

robotics_easier_than_cs = 'Yes' ('JHU CS is competitive; ME + minor is less gated') is unsupported. CS declaration uses an SIS form, a four-year plan and department approval, with no published GPA or capacity gate. All majors except BME are equally open after admission.
Electronics Design Lab is EN.520.468 in the 2026-27 EE catalog. The '520.448' in the existing course list comes from older LCSR and focus-area pages.

The existing recommendation (BS CS + AI/ML sequence + minor) is changed to ECE. ECE has a formal catalog Robotics focus area that covers controls, embedded systems, perception, mechatronics and the CS robotics courses. The gates for the two majors are identical.
Undergrad robotics teams are not limited to the Robotics Club. The Hopkinauts Mars Rover Team (University Rover Challenge) is also active (JHU giving story, July 2025).
The LCSR 'BS/MSE' is a combined five-year BS + MSE in Robotics that current JHU undergrads apply to in junior or senior year. It is not a robotics bachelor's degree.

nc-state.name: North Carolina State University
nc-state.recommended_summary: Apply to the College of Engineering (all first-years enter Engineering First Year), list Electrical Engineering as the intended major, then CODA into the BS in Electrical Engineering and declare the Controls and Robotics Concentration, the only named robotics program on the Raleigh campus.

bs_robotics.notes: No bachelor's degree with Robotics in its title at NC State Raleigh in the 2026-27 catalog. The closest thing is the Joint NC State/UNC Asheville BS in Engineering, Mechatronics Concentration (JEM). It is ABET EAC accredited but taught all four years on the UNC Asheville campus; students apply to UNC Asheville, not NC State Raleigh. A March 2026 NC State article says faculty plan an interdisciplinary robotics minor first and possibly a robotics major later; neither exists yet.

ece.home_unit: College of Engineering, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
ece.robotics_track: Controls and Robotics Concentration (BS Electrical Engineering)
ece.entry: All first-years are admitted to Engineering First Year (EFY), not to ECE. After the CODA courses (MA 141, MA 241, PY 205, CH 101, CH 102 at C or better, plus ENG 101, E 101, E 115), students apply through CODA, earliest in December of year one; seats are capped per department and applicants are ranked by CODA GPA.
ece.notes: The concentration is 24 hours: MA 305 (or MA 405) and ECE 308 required, 6 hours chosen from ECE 411, ECE 425/525, ECE 441, ECE 455, ECE 460/560, and 12 open hours from the ECE elective list. It sits inside the BSEE only; Computer Engineering has no robotics concentration (its closest is the Embedded Systems Concentration). The CODA guarantee is entry to at least one program with open seats, not to a first choice. ECE says no second CODA is needed to switch majors within ECE. ECE 456 Mechatronics exists in the course catalog but is not on the ECE elective list, so check with an advisor before counting it.

cs.home_unit: College of Engineering, Department of Computer Science
cs.robotics_track: Undergraduate Track in Robotics (CSC elective track, recognized by a letter of completion, not a transcript concentration)

key_courses.title: Introduction to Internet of Things (IoT) Systems

cs.entry: Same as ECE: admitted to Engineering First Year, then apply to Computer Science through CODA after the required first-year courses, competing for a capped number of seats ranked by CODA GPA.
cs.notes: Formal transcript concentrations are Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Game Development and Software Engineering; none is robotics. The Robotics Track uses four CSC restricted electives (12 hours): required CSC 495 special topics in robot motion planning and software engineering for robotics plus CSC 422, and one elective (e.g. CSC 453 or CSC 495 Introduction to Mobile Robotics). A 2.5 major GPA earns a completion letter. The track page states AI Concentration students are not eligible for it. The BS CS is ABET CAC (computing), not EAC. 2025-26 combined CODA data: 186 EFY first-choice applicants, 185 taken, CODA GPA middle 50% 3.27-3.87.

nc-state.ecosystem: College of Engineering Robotics Initiative (launched 2025, launch director Helen Huang, with the CLEAR Core and planned robotics space in Engineering Building II and Research Building IV), and student teams RoboPack, BattlePack Combat Robotics and AquaPack.
nc-state.tradeoff: The student is not admitted to ECE as a freshman: he must earn a strong CODA GPA in year one to win a capped EE seat, and the robotics concentration is controls- and hardware-heavy, with less robot software and perception than the CS Robotics Track.
corrections_to_existing: CODA Success courses: from Spring 2026 PY 205 is a 4-credit course and PY 206 is no longer required when the 4-credit PY 205 is taken; the EE catalog lists MA 141, MA 241, CH 101, CH 102 and PY 205 as CODA courses.
The existing plan to take the CS AI Concentration conflicts with robotics: the CSC Robotics Track page states AI Concentration students are not eligible for the Robotics Track.

CS has four concentrations in the 2026-27 catalog (AI, Cybersecurity, Game Development, Software Engineering), plus non-transcript elective tracks in Security, Entrepreneurship and Robotics; the existing data omits the Robotics Track.
Robot Motion Planning appears as ECE 441/CSC 441 (cross-listed) and separately as CSC 451; the CS degree's restricted elective list names CSC 451, not CSC 441.
ECE 456 Mechatronics is not on the published ECE elective list, so it is not a guaranteed part of the Controls and Robotics Concentration.

ECE 555 Autonomous Robot Systems and ECE 516 System Control Engineering are graduate courses (graduate courses need a 3.5 GPA for undergrads); they should not be counted as core undergraduate robotics courses.

Latest CODA figures are 2025-26: CS EFY 186 first-choice applicants, 185 taken, CODA GPA middle 50% 3.27-3.87 (the 2024-25 CS numbers in the existing data are a year old). EE and CpE 2025-26 sheets could not be opened, so the EE-vs-CS comparison is not re-verified.

The claim that students must CODA into EE/CpE to take 300-level ECE courses was not found on current ECE pages; the ECE tour page says only that EFY students get registration priority for ECE classes.
Robotics minor: none exists yet; a March 2026 NC State article says an interdisciplinary robotics minor is being planned.

Mechatronics Engineering is listed in ecs_robotics_alt as run 'from Fall 2024'. That date is unverified, and the program is not ABET-accredited per the Clark School catalog.
Fall 2027 rules: EE and CpE are high-demand majors and the LEP page says admission to them is not guaranteed even after the 45-credit gateway review (checked again 13 Oct 2026).

michigan.name: University of Michigan, Ann Arbor
michigan.recommended_summary: Apply to the College of Engineering and plan to declare the B.S.E. in Robotics. It is a real first-year-reachable robotics major with no published cap, and it avoids the CS selection gate.

bs_robotics.entry: First-years apply to the College of Engineering, not to Robotics. After at least one full term on campus, with a 2.0 U-M GPA, good standing, and a C or better in intro linear algebra, programming or design, calculus, and physics or chemistry, they book a declaration appointment with Robotics advising.
bs_robotics.notes: Launched Fall 2022. More than 175 declared majors. Declaring requires meeting eligibility rules, not a competitive selection; no cap is published. The College of Engineering degree table lists it as not ABET-accredited (EE and Computer Engineering are EAC-accredited). Five optional concentrations start Fall 2026: Perception and Reasoning, Dynamics and Control, Hardware and Sensors, Human-Robot Interaction, and Full Stack Robotic Systems. External transfers can enter Robotics directly starting Winter 2026. Core includes ROB 204, three of six 300-level core courses (ROB 310, 311, 314, 320, 330, 340), and the ROB 450 Robotics Capstone; 128 credits.

ece.home_unit: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (ECE Division), College of Engineering
ece.entry: First-years are admitted to the College of Engineering and declare EE or Computer Engineering under the standard college rules: one full term, 2.0 GPA, good standing, C or better in calculus, physics or chemistry, and intro engineering courses. No advance selection is required.
ece.notes: No formal robotics concentration was found for EE or Computer Engineering; the EECS bulletin lists control systems among EE concentration areas. EECS 367 is cross-listed as ROB 380, EECS 464 as ROB 464, and EECS 465 as ROB 422, so ECE students take the same robotics courses as Robotics majors. Both degrees are ABET EAC-accredited. The EE major page could not be opened to confirm its current list of paths.

cs.entry: Apply to Engineering or LSA and request advance selection for CS on the Common App. Official U-M pages say students admitted Fall 2023 or later must be selected for CS before declaring; those not selected can apply later as Enrolled Discoverers (April 1 to May 16, limited capacity).
cs.notes: Selection status for Fall 2027 is unclear. The CoE bulletin, CSE pages and a U-M advising article updated August 2026 still describe selection. But a Michigan Daily headline says CS no longer requires a specialized application, and the LSA CS major page for Winter 2026 drops the selection language. The article could not be opened, so confirm with CSE advising before applying. No formal robotics track exists in CS. Whether every course listed counts as an upper-level CS elective was not checked against the program guide. The B.S.E. in Computer Science is not ABET-accredited.

michigan.ecosystem: The Robotics Department is based in the Ford Motor Company Robotics Building, with a Mars Yard outside used by the Michigan Mars Rover student team.
michigan.tradeoff: The Robotics B.S.E. is not ABET-accredited, unlike EE and Computer Engineering. It is also not a direct admit, so the student must first get into the College of Engineering and meet first-term course and GPA rules before declaring.

wpi.name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute
wpi.recommended_summary: Apply intending the BS in Robotics Engineering: it is a full, ABET (EAC)-accredited primary major with a four-course Unified Robotics core, and WPI lets first-years declare it with no published gate.

bs_robotics.degree_name: Bachelor of Science in Robotics Engineering
bs_robotics.entry: Students apply to WPI as a whole through one first-year application, then declare a major near the end of B-Term (about mid-first-year). No GPA cutoff or capacity limit for declaring is published.
bs_robotics.notes: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under General Criteria. Core is RBE 2001, 2002, 3001 and 3002, plus a robotics MQP capstone, 1 unit of CS, 2/3 unit of ECE (embedded systems), statics and classical controls. Strictly speaking WPI admits to the university, not the major; 'direct admit' here means a first-year can declare RBE freely. Program start year and enrollment size were not verified on WPI pages.

cs.entry: Same as all WPI majors: admitted to the university, then declare CS (or AI) near the end of B-Term of the first year. No published gate.
cs.notes: The CS catalog has no computer vision or robotics course; RBE 4540, RBE 4701 and RBE 4744 appear on the CS major page only under the science/engineering requirement, not the CS requirement. The BS AI appears to be new (WPI announced it in early 2026; launch year not confirmed). CS ABET status was not verified.

robotics_minor.name: Minor in Robotics Engineering
robotics_minor.open_to: Non-RBE majors (e.g. CS, ECE, ME, BME); 2 units including RBE 1001, 2001, 2002 and one 3000+ RBE capstone; no more than 1 unit may overlap the major.

wpi.ecosystem: A standalone Robotics Engineering Department with 15 listed labs (e.g. PeAR Lab, Soft Robotics Lab, MER Lab) plus PracticePoint, and undergrad teams including the WPI Robotics Club's VEXU and Combat Robotics teams and an MQP team that reached the 2024 NASA Lunabotics finals.
wpi.tradeoff: RBE is broad and interdisciplinary, so it gives less depth in circuits/signals than ECE or in algorithms/software than CS; students wanting that depth often add a CS or ECE minor.
corrections_to_existing: Several RBE course titles are wrong. 2026-27 catalog: RBE 2001 is 'Unified Robotics I: Mechanical Applications in Robotics'; RBE 2002 is 'Unified Robotics II: Sensing and Perception in Robotics'; RBE 2020 is 'Embedded Systems for Robotics'; RBE 3100 is 'Social Implications of Robotics'; RBE 4540 is 'Vision-based Robotic Manipulation'; RBE 4601 is 'Human Factors and Human-Robot Interface'; RBE 4701 is 'Artificial Intelligence for Robotics'; RBE 4744 is 'Deep Learning for Perception'.
'RBE 100X Foundations of Robotics' is not in the 2026-27 catalog. RBE 4322/ME 4322 'Modeling and Analysis of Mechatronic Systems' is missing from the list.

The existing data contradicts itself ('DIRECT' vs 'NOT direct-admit'). The fact: WPI admits to the university and students declare any major, including RBE, near the end of B-Term of year one with no published gate.
'RBE is meaningfully less oversubscribed than CS' is not supported by any WPI source; WPI publishes no per-major admit or declaration data.
Recommended route for robotics should be the BS Robotics Engineering, not the BS Artificial Intelligence (the BS AI does have a Robotics concentration).
The Robotics Engineering minor is aimed at non-RBE majors (2 units, max 1 unit overlap with the major), not 'alongside the BS'.
Start year 2007 and 374 majors were not verified on WPI pages; the BS page now cites 17+ robotics research groups (department research page lists 15).
